reading.body:
The directory covers 450 AI tools across 23 categories, with 63 in-depth profiles that include pricing, strengths, weaknesses, and governance notes.

The catalog is broad but shallow by design. Only 63 of the 450 tools get the full treatment, so the remaining 387 are listed without the pricing and governance detail that makes the profiled entries useful. A reader comparing vendors should treat the 63 profiles as the evidence base and the rest as an index.

The governance notes are the part that connects to the site's larger argument. Tools that carry governance detail are the ones a buyer can actually evaluate against procurement and compliance requirements, and that detail is what separates a directory entry from a purchasing decision. Nothing here speaks to compute, buildings, or power, and the data does not claim otherwise.

What the data does not cover: it gives no breakdown of how the 450 split between commercial and open source, no update history beyond the single verified date, and no indication of how the 63 profiles were chosen. The refresh interval is seven days, so the counts are current as of the verified date and no further.
